summary: The PDF supports each part of the assignment coding for S1 and S2: students were 'randomly assigned to either the control group or the experiment (ChatGPT-3.5) group within each discipline and before their respective class' (PDF p. 7), the experiment arm got ChatGPT-3.5 for its own 15-minute ideation task, and the control arm used its usual resources under an instruction not to use any generative AI, in a between-subjects design. The caveats change no coded value: the paper never describes the randomization method or prints per-arm counts, assignment preceded consent and exclusions (Table 1's standard errors imply unequal analyzed Marketing arms), and control students could use internet searches.
